snip.t: Filariasis: Diethylcarbamazine (DEC) for lymphatic filariasis; ivermectin for onchocerciasis.
Vector: Onchocerca volvulus → river blindness (onchocerciasis); S. metallicum → Mansonella ozzardi (non-pathogenic)
Glossina = tsetse fly (African trypanosomiasis); Simulium = onchocerciasis; Ixodes = Lyme disease.

| Diethylcarbamazine (DEC) | Immobilises microfilariae + enhances immune recognition | Lymphatic filariasis (Wuchereria bancrofti, Brugia) · loiasis · tropical eosinophilia | Mazzotti-like reaction · contraindicated in onchocerciasis (can cause ocular damage) |
| Ivermectin key use | Onchocerciasis (river blindness) · Strongyloides · scabies |
Write short notes on Onchocerciasis (River Blindness) Control.

qs.q: Black flies of the genus Simulium are implicated in onchocerciasis. What is their preferred larval breeding site?
o: Stagnant and polluted urban water body habitats
Clean and artificial container water sources
Brackish and coastal tidal pool environments
Deep and anaerobic swamp water locations
qs.e: Simulium larvae require fast-flowing, well-oxygenated water, typically found in mountain streams or rapids.

qs.q: Which of the following transmits parasites for river blindness (Onchocerciasis)?
qs.e: River blindness is caused by the filarial worm Onchocerca volvulus, which is transmitted by the bite of infected blackflies (genus Simulium).
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: Microbiology Exam - September 25, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: The black fly (Simulium species) transmits the parasitic nematode Onchocerca volvulus, which causes river blindness (onchocerciasis).
qs.e: Black flies, belonging to the genus Simulium, are the vectors for the parasite Onchocerca volvulus, the causative agent of onchocerciasis, commonly known as river blindness. This disease is prevalent in parts of Africa and Latin America.

qs.q: Which of the following transmits the parasitic nematodes responsible for river blindness (onchocerciasis)?

qs.q: Which of the following arthropods is the primary vector for transmitting parasites that cause river blindness (onchocerciasis)?
qs.e: Onchocerciasis is transmitted by the bite of infected female black flies (Simulium species), which breed in fast-flowing rivers and streams.
